key_insight: Surrogate-assisted genetic programming learns scheduling rules across changing tasks while reducing catastrophic forgetting.
engineering_relevance: The method targets adaptive production scheduling in dynamic flexible job shops, rather than solid mechanics or constitutive modeling.
method: Adaptive two-stage training balances learning new tasks with retaining prior knowledge.
Task-similarity weighting regulates knowledge reuse across sequential scheduling tasks.
A distance-constrained surrogate model improves fitness estimation accuracy.
evidence_signal: Experiments on sequential heterogeneous scheduling tasks with job or batch arrivals report reduced forgetting and stronger adaptability than several comparison methods.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative gains or computational costs, limiting assessment of practical deployment benefits.
paper_title: Lifelong Learning of Scheduling Rules with Surrogate-assisted Genetic Programming for Dynamic Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
